questions.question: If 5,000 children were surveyed, how many have bedtimes that are 10:30 p.m. or earlier, according to the circle graph above?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 220 245" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif"><text x="110" y="16" font-size="12" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222">WEEKNIGHT BEDTIMES, AGE 11</text><g transform="translate(0,20)"><path d="M110,110 L110.0,15.0 A95,95 0 0 1 204.8,116.0 Z" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M110,110 L204.8,116.0 A95,95 0 0 1 170.6,183.2 Z" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M110,110 L170.6,183.2 A95,95 0 0 1 92.2,203.3 Z" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M110,110 L92.2,203.3 A95,95 0 0 1 16.7,127.8 Z" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.5"/><path d="M110,110 L16.7,127.8 A95,95 0 0 1 110.0,15.0 Z" fill="none" stroke="#333" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="152.9" y="69.7" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222"><tspan x="152.9" dy="0" font-weight="700">26%</tspan><tspan x="152.9" dy="12">10:30 p.m.</tspan></text><text x="162.5" y="136.7" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222"><tspan x="162.5" dy="0" font-weight="700">13%</tspan><tspan x="162.5" dy="12">10 p.m.</tspan></text><text x="124.6" y="167.0" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222"><tspan x="124.6" dy="0" font-weight="700">14%</tspan><tspan x="124.6" dy="12">Earlier than</tspan><tspan x="124.6" dy="12">10 p.m.</tspan></text><text x="68.4" y="151.6" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222"><tspan x="68.4" dy="0" font-weight="700">19%</tspan><tspan x="68.4" dy="12">No bedtime</tspan></text><text x="64.6" y="72.5" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle" fill="#222"><tspan x="64.6" dy="0" font-weight="700">28%</tspan><tspan x="64.6" dy="12">11 p.m. or later</tspan></text></g></svg>

solution.exhibit_text:
Read the question carefully—"10:30 p.m. or earlier" includes 10:30 p.m., 10 p.m., and earlier than 10 p.m. Refer to the circle graph to find the percentages: 26% + 13% + 14% = 53% of the children surveyed have bedtimes that are 10:30 p.m. or earlier. Finally, find 53% of 5,000.

\[\dfrac{53}{100} \times 5{,}000 = \dfrac{265{,}000}{100} = 2{,}650\]

questions.question: What is the circumference of the circle inscribed in the square above?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 140 120" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif"><rect x="10" y="10" width="100" height="100" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><circle cx="60" cy="60" r="50" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="122" y="64" font-size="13" fill="#222">6</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text: Recall that the circumference of a circle is \(\pi\) times its diameter. If the circle is inscribed in a square with a side length of 6, it must have a diameter of 6. Therefore, the circle has a circumference of \(6\pi\).

questions.question: For what value of \(s\) is \(\dfrac{249-s}{14} = 17\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Isolate the variable, paying careful attention to signs.

\[\dfrac{249-s}{14} = 17\]
\[249 - s = 238\]
\[-s = -11\]
\[s = 11\]

questions.question: In the figure described above, ABCD is a rectangle with length 12 cm and width 8 cm. Points W, X, Y, and Z are the midpoints of the sides. What is the area of the shaded quadrilateral?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 175 135" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif"><rect x="20" y="20" width="120" height="80" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><polygon points="80,20 140,60 80,100 20,60" fill="#ccc" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="14" y="16" font-size="11">A</text><text x="80" y="16" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">W</text><text x="144" y="16" font-size="11">B</text><text x="144" y="56" font-size="11">X</text><text x="144" y="112" font-size="11">C</text><text x="80" y="114" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">Y</text><text x="10" y="112" font-size="11">D</text><text x="6" y="56" font-size="11">Z</text><text x="80" y="128" font-size="11" text-anchor="middle">12 cm</text><text x="146" y="75" font-size="11">8 cm</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text:
Since W, X, Y, and Z are the midpoints of the rectangle's sides, drawing a vertical line connecting the top and bottom midpoints and a horizontal line connecting the side midpoints creates 4 congruent rectangles. Each rectangle consists of 2 identical triangles with a base of \(12 \div 2 = 6\) cm and a height of \(8 \div 2 = 4\) cm.

Because there are 8 identical triangles and exactly 4 of them are shaded, the area of the shaded area is half the area of the rectangle. The area of the rectangle is the length times the width, which is \(12 \text{ cm} \times 8 \text{ cm} = 96\) sq cm. Therefore, the area of the shaded quadrilateral is \(\dfrac{1}{2} \times 96 = 48\) sq cm.

The distance between the two points is the positive difference between their coordinates, or \(5 - (-7) = 12\).

questions.question:
What is the value of the expression shown below?
\[200(1-0.4)^2+28=\]

solution.exhibit_text: Evaluate the expression using PEMDAS. First, perform the subtraction inside the parentheses: \(1 - 0.4 = 0.6\). Square the result: \((0.6)^2 = 0.36\). Multiply the result by 200: \(200(0.36) = 72\). Finally, add 28: \(72 + 28 = 100\).

questions.question: Erin has a box of quarters from various states in the Northeast. The box contains 6 quarters from New York, 4 from Pennsylvania, 2 from Delaware, and 3 from New Jersey. If Erin selects 2 quarters at random from this box, without replacing them, what is the probability that both coins are **not** from New York?

solution.exhibit_text:
Since Erin does not replace the coins, you must pay careful attention to the number of coins each time she chooses a coin. The total number of quarters in the box to start is \(6+4+2+3=15\). The number of quarters that are not from New York is \(4+2+3=9\).

The probability that the first quarter is not from New York is \(\dfrac{9}{15}\), or \(\dfrac{3}{5}\). Now, out of the 14 remaining quarters, there are 8 quarters left that are not from New York. The probability that the second quarter is not from New York is \(\dfrac{8}{14}\), or \(\dfrac{4}{7}\).

Multiply these two probabilities to find the probability that both coins are not from New York:

\[\dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{4}{7} = \dfrac{12}{35}\]

questions.question:
At a coffee shop, 24 pastries were served yesterday to 200 breakfast customers. Today, 18 pastries were served to breakfast customers. Assuming that the pastry sale rate is the same for both days, which proportions can be used to determine how many breakfast customers were served today?
Select the **three** correct answers.

solution.exhibit_text:
Let \(x\) be the number of breakfast customers served today. The ratio \(\dfrac{24 \text{ pastries}}{200 \text{ customers}}\) reflects the rate of 24 pastries for 200 customers yesterday. Set up a proportion to solve for \(x\), keeping pastries in the numerators and customers in the denominators: \(\dfrac{24 \text{ pastries}}{200 \text{ customers}} = \dfrac{18 \text{ pastries}}{x \text{ customers}}\). This proportion matches (C). Evaluate the remaining answer choices by cross multiplying to see which are equivalent to \((24)(x) = (200)(18)\).

(A): \((24)(18) = (x)(200)\) is not equivalent to \((24)(x)=(200)(18)\); eliminate.
(B): \((200)(18) = (24)(x)\) is equivalent to \((24)(x)=(200)(18)\); correct.
(D): \((24)(x) = (18)(200)\) is equivalent to \((24)(x)=(200)(18)\); correct.
(E): \((x)(200) = (24)(18)\) is not equivalent to \((24)(x)=(200)(18)\); eliminate.

questions.question: In the set of consecutive integers from 10 to 40, inclusive, how many integers are multiples of neither 3 nor 4?

solution.exhibit_text:
There are \(40 - 10 + 1 = 31\) integers between 10 and 40, inclusive. You must add 1 because simply subtracting \(40-10\) gives the numbers *between* the two endpoints of 10 and 40. Here, you are told that the endpoints are included. To determine the number of integers that are multiples of neither 3 nor 4, determine the number of integers that *are* multiples of 3, 4, or both, and subtract this from the total of 31.

A number is a multiple of 3 if it is divisible by 3, so the multiples of 3 between 10 and 40, inclusive, are 12, 15, 18, 21, 24, 27, 30, 33, 36, and 39. There are 10 numbers in this list. Using similar logic, the multiples of 4 between 10 and 40, inclusive, are 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36, and 40. There are 8 numbers in this list. However, observe that the numbers 12, 24, and 36 appear on both lists. Therefore, there are \(10+8-3=15\) numbers that are multiples of 3, 4, or both.

Thus, there are \(31-15=16\) integers between 10 and 40 inclusive that are multiples of neither 3 nor 4.

questions.question: In pentagon ABCDE shown above, each side is 1 centimeter. If a particle starts at point A and travels clockwise 723 centimeters along ABCDE, at which point will the particle stop?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 170 190" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif"><polygon points="27.9,76.5 85.0,35.0 142.1,76.5 120.3,143.5 49.7,143.5" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="13.9" y="74.5" font-size="13" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">A</text><text x="85.0" y="21.0" font-size="13" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">B</text><text x="156.1" y="74.5" font-size="13" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">C</text><text x="134.3" y="159.5" font-size="13" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">D</text><text x="33.7" y="159.5" font-size="13" font-weight="700" text-anchor="middle">E</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text: If the particle travels from A to B to C to D to E and then back to A, it has traveled 5 centimeters, since each side of the pentagon measures 1 centimeter. If it goes all the way around the pentagon again, it has traveled another 5 centimeters, for a total of 10 centimeters. In fact, every time the particle makes a complete revolution around the pentagon (from point A back to point A again), it travels an additional 5 centimeters. So, if the number of centimeters the particle has traveled is a multiple of 5, the particle must be at point A. The number 723 is 3 more than a multiple of 5. If the particle had gone 720 centimeters it would be at point A; since it has gone 3 more centimeters, it must be at point D.

questions.question: The spare change on a dresser is composed of pennies, nickels, and dimes. If the ratio of pennies to nickels is 2:3 and the ratio of pennies to dimes is 3:4, what is the ratio of nickels to dimes?

solution.exhibit_text: Don't fall into the "obvious answer" trap of just taking the numbers of nickels and dimes from the two ratios to come up with 3:4. To find the ratio of nickels to dimes, you need to get the two ratios in proportion to one another by getting the same number of pennies in each. Multiplying the first ratio (pennies to nickels) by 3 gives you 6:9; multiplying the second ratio (pennies to dimes) by 2 gives you 6:8. Since the number corresponding to pennies is now the same in each ratio (6), the ratio of nickels to dimes can now be found. The ratio of nickels to dimes is 9:8.

questions.question: How many positive integers satisfy the inequality \(19-2x>4\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Isolate \(x\), remembering that you must flip the inequality when multiplying or dividing by a negative number.

\[19-2x>4\]
\[-2x>-15\]
\[x<\dfrac{15}{2}\]

The improper fraction \(\dfrac{15}{2}\) is equivalent to 7.5. The question is asking how many positive integers are less than 7.5. The integers that satisfy this are 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7. This is a total of 7 integers, so enter **7**.

questions.question: Margo bowled a mean of 110 points per game in her first 4 games. In her 5th game, she bowled 160 points. What is her mean score for the first 5 games?

solution.exhibit_text:
Margo bowled a mean of 110 points per game in each of the first 4 games, so she earned a total of \(110 \times 4 = 440\) points for the first 4 games. Use this information to calculate the mean over the first 5 games:

\[\dfrac{440+160}{5} = \dfrac{600}{5} = 120\]

questions.question: A water storage tank currently contains 2,400 liters of water. If this amount fills the tank to exactly \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of its total capacity, how many **kiloliters** of water must be added to fill the tank completely?

solution.exhibit_text:
Let the total capacity of the water tank be \(x\). The question says that 2,400 liters of water fill the tank to \(\dfrac{3}{5}\) of its capacity. Therefore, \(2{,}400 = \dfrac{3}{5}x\). Solve for \(x\) to determine the total capacity of the tank: \(2{,}400 \times 5 = 3x\) and \(x = \dfrac{2{,}400 \times 5}{3} = 800 \times 5 = 4{,}000\) liters. The question asks how many kiloliters of water must be added to fill the tank completely. The tank needs an additional \(4{,}000-2{,}400=1{,}600\) liters. There are 1,000 liters in 1 kiloliter. Therefore:

\[1{,}600 \text{ liters} \times \left(\dfrac{1 \text{ kiloliter}}{1{,}000 \text{ liters}}\right) = 1.6 \text{ kiloliters}\]

questions.question: In a certain tourism destination, 28% of the city's residents work in the hospitality industry. 55% of residents are age 40 or younger, and 15% of residents are people age 40 or younger who work in the hospitality industry. What percentage of the employed population are people older than 40 who do **not** work in the hospitality industry?

solution.exhibit_text: Read word problems carefully to sort through the information they give you. Here, the question asks for residents older than 40 who do *not* work in hospitality. First, find the percent of residents older than 40: the problem tells you the percent of residents age 40 or younger (55%), so you can subtract from 100 to get 45% of the population is older than 40. To find how many of these residents *don't* work in hospitality, you need to know how many *do*, which the problem doesn't tell you. However, it does tell you how many total residents work in hospitality (28%) and how many of those are 40 or younger (15%), so you can subtract to find residents over 40 who work in hospitality: \(28\%-15\%=13\%\). Finally, subtract over-40 residents in hospitality from all over-40 residents: \(45\%-13\%=32\%\) of residents are older than 40 and *don't* work in hospitality.

questions.question: Which inequality is equivalent to \(-2(x+4) \le 10\)?

solution.exhibit_text: First, distribute the \(-2\): \(-2x-8 \le 10\). Then add 8 to both sides: \(-2x \le 18\). Now isolate \(x\) by dividing both sides by \(-2\). Remember that you must flip the inequality sign when you divide by a negative. \(18 \div -2 = -9\), so \(x \ge -9\).

questions.question: The average of five consecutive multiples of 5 is 20. What is the **largest** of these numbers?

solution.exhibit_text: The average of a set of evenly-spaced numbers is equal to the median (middle number) of the set. Since the average of five consecutive multiples of 5 is 20, the median equals 20: __, __, 20, __, __. Adding 5 twice to 20 will give you the largest of these numbers, which is 30.

questions.question: In the triangle above, if the measure of \(\angle ABC\) is \(60\degree\), then what is the value of \(y\)?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 300 130" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif"><polygon points="20,110 115,22 290,110" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="10" y="122" font-size="12" font-weight="700">A</text><text x="112" y="16" font-size="12" font-weight="700">B</text><text x="292" y="122" font-size="12" font-weight="700">C</text><text x="118" y="42" font-size="11">(2x-4)°</text><text x="34" y="100" font-size="11">(3y)°</text><text x="255" y="100" font-size="11">y°</text></svg>

solution.exhibit_text: In the figure, \(\angle ABC\) is labeled \((2x-4)\degree\), and in the question stem, you're told that \(\angle ABC\) measures \(60\degree\). So, \(2x-4=60\), which leads to \(2x=64\) and \(x=32\). That means that \(\angle BAC\), which is labeled \((3x)\degree\), must measure \(3 \times 32\), or \(96\degree\). Since the measures of the angles of a triangle must add up to \(180\degree\), \(60\degree+96\degree+y\degree=180\degree\), and \(y=24\).

questions.question: A rectangular quilt is 9 feet long and 6 feet wide. It is constructed entirely of square fabric patches measuring 0.75 foot on each side. How many fabric patches are needed to make the quilt?

solution.exhibit_text:
This question can be solved by dividing the area of the quilt by the area of a patch. First, determine the area of the quilt: \(6 \times 9 = 54\) square feet. Next, find the area of one patch. It is helpful to rewrite 0.75 as a fraction: \(\dfrac{75}{100} = \dfrac{3}{4}\). The area of one patch is \(\dfrac{3}{4} \times \dfrac{3}{4} = \dfrac{9}{16}\) square feet.

Now, divide the two to get the number of patches needed (remembering that dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal):

\[54 \div \dfrac{9}{16} = 54 \times \dfrac{16}{9} = \dfrac{54}{9} \times 16 = 6 \times 16 = 96\]

questions.question:
\[Q=\dfrac{R}{3}=S-6=7T=\dfrac{U}{10}>0\]
According to the statement above, which variable has the **least** value?

solution.exhibit_text:
Because it's easiest to compare these quantities if you have numbers instead of variables, pick a simple number to substitute for \(Q\), like 2. Take each piece of the equation at a time and solve for each of the answer choices:

\[Q=\dfrac{R}{3} \Rightarrow 2=\dfrac{R}{3} \Rightarrow R=6\]
\[Q=S-6 \Rightarrow 2=S-6 \Rightarrow S=8\]
\[Q=7T \Rightarrow 2=7T \Rightarrow T=\dfrac{2}{7}\]
\[Q=\dfrac{U}{10} \Rightarrow 2=\dfrac{U}{10} \Rightarrow U=20\]

The only fraction and thus the smallest number is \(T\).

questions.question: At summer camp, campers are randomly assigned to one of 25 cabins and one of 4 cafeterias. Josef likes 8 of the cabins and 2 of the cafeterias. What is the probability that he is assigned to both a cabin and a cafeteria that he likes?

solution.exhibit_text: To find the probability that Josef likes *both* the cabin and the cafeteria he is assigned, find the probability of each and multiply the results. The probability that he will be assigned one of the 8 out of 25 cabins that he likes is \(\dfrac{8}{25}\), and the probability that he will be assigned one of the 2 out of 4 cafeterias that he likes is \(\dfrac{2}{4}\). The product is \(\dfrac{8}{25} \times \dfrac{2}{4} = \dfrac{16}{100}\), or 16%.

questions.question: Over a one-month period, a software team is assigned a total of 250 tasks for a new application. The table above shows the first three phases of tasks within the larger project. What percentage of the 250 tasks is the **total** number of tasks in these first three phases?
questions.figure_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 260 110" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" font-family="system-ui,sans-serif"><text x="8" y="16" font-size="12" font-weight="700">PROJECT MILESTONES</text><g transform="translate(8,26)" font-size="11"><rect x="0" y="0" width="244" height="72" fill="none" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><line x1="50" y1="0" x2="50" y2="72" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><line x1="0" y1="18" x2="244" y2="18" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><line x1="0" y1="36" x2="244" y2="36" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><line x1="0" y1="54" x2="244" y2="54" stroke="#222" stroke-width="1"/><text x="6" y="13" font-weight="700">Phase</text><text x="58" y="13" font-weight="700">Tasks Assigned</text><text x="6" y="31">I</text><text x="58" y="31">1-12, inclusive</text><text x="6" y="49">II</text><text x="58" y="49">20-34, inclusive</text><text x="6" y="67">III</text><text x="58" y="67">42-60, inclusive</text></g></svg>

solution.exhibit_text:
To find the percentage, you must first calculate the total number of tasks in the three phases and then divide by the total project size. Because the ranges are inclusive, use the formula End − Start + 1.

Phase I: \((12-1)+1=12\)
Phase II: \((34-20)+1=15\)
Phase III: \((60-42)+1=19\)

Thus, the total number of tasks for these three phases is \(12+15+19=46\). Use \(\text{Percent}=\dfrac{\text{Part}}{\text{Whole}}\times 100\%\) to calculate the percentage:

\[\dfrac{46}{250}\times 100\% = \dfrac{46}{250}\times\dfrac{4}{4}\times 100\%\]
\[=\dfrac{184}{1{,}000}\times 100\%\]
\[=\dfrac{184}{10}\%\]
\[=18.4\%\]

questions.question: How many negative **odd** numbers satisfy the inequality \(4x+100 \ge 20\)?

solution.exhibit_text:
Solve the inequality for \(x\). To do this, subtract 100 from both sides of the inequality and then divide both sides by 4.

\[4x+100 \ge 20\]
\[4x \ge -80\]
\[x \ge -20\]

Don't answer too quickly—the answer isn't 19 or 20. List the negative **odd** numbers that are greater than or equal to \(-20\). The set includes \(-19, -17, -15, -13, -11, -9, -7, -5, -3\), and \(-1\). There are 10 of them.

questions.question: The perimeter of a square A is three times the perimeter of an equilateral triangle B. What is the ratio of the length of one side of square A to the length of one side of equilateral triangle B?

solution.exhibit_text:
To find the ratio of the side lengths, set up an algebraic relationship based on the perimeters. The perimeter of a square with side \(s_A\) is \(4s_A\), and the perimeter of an equilateral triangle with side \(s_B\) is \(3s_B\). Translating "the perimeter of the square is three times the perimeter of the triangle" into math gives \(4s_A = 3(3s_B)\), which simplifies to \(4s_A = 9s_B\). Obtain the ratio of the side lengths \(\dfrac{s_A}{s_B}\) by dividing both sides by 4 and then by \(s_B\):

\[\dfrac{s_A}{s_B} = \dfrac{9s_B}{4} \Big/ s_B\]
\[\dfrac{s_A}{s_B} = \dfrac{9}{4}\]

questions.question: Point P is **not** on line \(m\). How many lines can be drawn through P that form a \(90\degree\) angle with line \(m\)?

options.D: Cannot be determined from the information given.

solution.exhibit_text:
Draw a picture to better visualize the situation.

As you can see, a line drawn from P perpendicular to line \(m\) will create two \(90\degree\) angles. However, a line drawn anywhere else will no longer be perpendicular and therefore will not create any \(90\degree\) angles, so only one line meets the conditions of the question.

questions.question: If Morgan drove 247 miles between 9:15 a.m. and 12:30 p.m. on the same day, what was her average speed in miles per hour?

solution.exhibit_text:
Start by finding out how long Morgan drove by counting the number of hours and quarter hours. Going from 9:15 a.m. to 12:15 p.m. is 3 hours, and from 12:15 to 12:30 is one quarter of an hour. Thus, Morgan's total driving time was 3.25 hours.

Next, divide the total distance traveled by the driving time to get the average speed: \(247 \div 3.25 = 76\). To make the division easier, you may want to divide 24,700 by 325.

Alternatively, you can use Backsolving. Start with (C). You are looking for a number that will get you to 247 when multiplied by 3.25: \(3.25 \times 67 = 217.75\). This is too small, and since (A) and (B) are smaller, you can also eliminate them, leaving only choice (D).

questions.question: A particular brand of asphalt used to pave driveways is made by mixing the following ingredients: 1 part asphalt cement, 12 parts sand, 4 parts gravel, and 3 parts porous stone. Covering one driveway requires 200 cubic feet of this asphalt. How many total cubic feet of sand are required to cover 6 identical driveways?

solution.exhibit_text:
Start by finding the total number of parts represented by the mixture. The ratio is 1:12:4:3, so the total number of parts is 20. Since there are 12 parts sand, the fraction of sand is:

\[\dfrac{12}{20} = \dfrac{3}{5}\]

Thus, the amount of sand in 200 cubic feet of asphalt (for 1 driveway) is:

\[\dfrac{3}{5} \times 200 = 120 \text{ cubic feet}\]

To cover 6 identical driveways, that would be \(120 \times 6 = 720\) cubic feet.

solution.exhibit_text:
Absolute value makes the output positive by ignoring the sign of the number. This means that the input can be either positive or negative. Thus, \(|x-2| \le 3\) implies both \(x-2 \le 3\) and \(-(x-2) \le 3\).

Rewriting the second inequality gives \(x-2 \ge -3\). Remember that the inequality sign flips when dividing or multiplying by a negative. Solve the first inequality for \(x\):

\[x-2 \le 3\]
\[x \le 3+2\]
\[x \le 5\]

Solve the second inequality for \(x\):

\[x-2 \ge -3\]
\[x \ge -3+2\]
\[x \ge -1\]

Thus, \(-1 \le x \le 5\). Since the symbol is \(\le\) (inclusive), use solid (closed) circles at \(-1\) and \(5\). The variable \(x\) is between \(-1\) and \(5\), so the line segment connecting these two points should be shaded.

Alternatively, use Backsolving. Since 0 is a solution for (C) and (D) but not in (A) and (B), let \(x=0\). When \(x\) is 0, \(|-2|\le 3\) is true. Thus, eliminate (A) and (B). Now, let \(x=4\). When \(x\) is 4, \(|4-2|\le 3\) is true. Thus, (D) is correct.

questions.question:
A cafe sells 1-gallon jugs of iced tea for $4.50. The cafe also sells lemonade in a 4-pack of 12-fluid-ounce bottles for $3.30.
Suppose the cafe wants to sell its lemonade in gallon containers instead. To the nearest dollar, how much more would a gallon of lemonade cost than a gallon of iced tea? (Note: 1 gallon = 128 fluid ounces).

solution.exhibit_text:
Find how much more a gallon of lemonade would cost than a gallon of iced tea. A gallon of iced tea costs $4.50, and a 4-pack of 12-fluid-ounce bottles of lemonade costs $3.30.

Lemonade comes in a 4-pack of 12-fluid-ounce bottles. This means that \(4 \times 12 = 48\) fluid ounces cost $3.30. A gallon contains 128 fluid ounces. Let \(x\) represent the price of 128 fluid ounces. Set up a proportion and cross-multiply to solve for \(x\):

\[\dfrac{48 \text{ ounces}}{\$3.30} = \dfrac{128 \text{ ounces}}{\$x}\]
\[48x = 128 \times 3.30\]
\[x = \dfrac{128 \times 3.30}{48} = \$8.80\]

Finally, subtract the two prices: \(\$8.80 - \$4.50 = \$4.30\). This is closest to 4, so (C) is correct.

questions.question:
Which of the following numbers has factors that include the smallest factor (other than 1) of 119?
Select the **two** correct answers.

solution.exhibit_text: Begin by listing the factors of 119: 1, 7, 17, and 119. The smallest factor (other than 1) is 7. Of the options listed (19, 27, 35, 40, and 63), only 35 \((5\times7)\) and 63 \((9\times7)\) have a factor of 7.
